svg.text: Everyday English - Idioms & slang
read the room
MEANING
Notice other people’s mood and reactions,
then adjust what you say or do.
IN CONTEXT
He read the room and saved his joke for a less
serious moment.
USAGE NOTE
Informal. Often used as advice or criticism:
Read the room. That direct command can
sound sharp; soften it when giving feedback.
CONVERSATION
A: Why did you stop telling that story?
B: I was trying to read the room. Everyone
looked uncomfortable.
A: So you changed direction rather than
pushing ahead?
B: Exactly. I asked whether they wanted to
discuss something else.
YOUR TURN
Describe a situation where noticing the mood
would change how you start a conversation.
